name: Can I build a new home on a small infill lot in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can a small infill lot in Los Angeles still work for a new custom home, and what are the usual constraints?
mainEntity.text: Can a small infill lot in Los Angeles still work for a new custom home, and what are the usual constraints?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small infill lot in Los Angeles can absolutely support a new custom home, but the design has to work within the site’s limits. The main constraints are setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, access, parking, utility placement, and privacy from neighboring homes. Small urban lots often demand more thoughtful design because every square foot matters. In some cases, a compact lot can still produce an excellent home if the layout is efficient and the massing is well planned. The challenge is cost: tight sites can be more expensive to build on because staging, access, and utility coordination are harder. Before moving forward, confirm that the program you want actually fits the parcel and that the project will not be compromised by code restrictions or awkward circulation. A feasibility study is the best first step.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small infill lot can work if zoning, setbacks, lot coverage, access, and utility placement allow the desired home size. Tight lots often require careful design to maximize square footage and privacy. The biggest risks are poor fit, parking challenges, and higher site development costs.
